ky.query: If an init hook modifies a nested object in the JSON body or the context, the change remains in the defaults and leaks into subsequent requests.
ky.query_en: Fix `init` hook mutations to nested `json` and `context` values leaking across requests `cloneInitHookOptions` shallow-cloned `json` and `context`, so an `init` hook that mutated a nested object or array in place (for example `options.json.user.id++`) changed the instance defaults and leaked into every later request. Nested `retry` arrays are already deep-cloned for exactly this reason, so the shortcoming was inconsistent.

ky.query: In init hooks, headers are undefined when none were passed, and adding one throws an error.
ky.query_en: Fix `init` hooks receiving `undefined` for `headers` when no headers were provided The docs promise that `options.headers` in `init` hooks is always a plain object, but it was `undefined` unless some option layer set headers. Adding a header in place in an `init` hook then threw.

ky.query: A query parameter removed by setting it to undefined stays in the URL if a later layer adds it again, so both the old and the new values are sent.
ky.query_en: Fix a search parameter removed with `undefined` staying in the input URL when a later layer re-adds it Re-adding a key in a later `searchParams` layer dropped the deletion marker, so the key was never removed from the input URL and the old value was sent alongside the new one. The marker now persists, and a merged `URLSearchParams` layer applies its own deletions before its entries so re-added values are kept.

ky.query: In Chromium, when the user aborts a request, the abort is mistaken for a network error and the request is retried.
ky.query_en: Fix a user abort in Chromium being reported as `NetworkError` and retried Chromium surfaces a user abort during a fetch or a body read as `TypeError: Failed to fetch` instead of an `AbortError`. Ky matched that message as a dropped connection, so an aborted request was wrapped in `NetworkError` and, for retriable methods, retried instead of failing. When a network-looking error arrives and the user-provided signal is aborted, Ky now throws the signal's reason instead, so a user abort surfaces consistently across runtimes, including custom reasons passed to `abort()`. This also makes the existi

ky.query: Passing the browser's native fetch function as an option causes the 'Illegal invocation' error.
ky.query_en: Fix `fetch: window.fetch` throwing "Illegal invocation" in browsers The `fetch` option was invoked as a method of Ky's internal options object, so a native `window.fetch` passed as-is was called with that object as `this`. Chromium rejects this with "Failed to execute 'fetch' on 'Window': Illegal invocation" and WebKit with "Can only call Window.fetch on instances of Window". The function is now called unbound, which native fetch accepts.

ky.query: If a custom fetch function throws immediately, the timeout timer stays active and then aborts the new retry attempt.
ky.query_en: Fix a stale timeout timer aborting the retried attempt when a custom `fetch` throws synchronously `timeout()` only cleared its timer through the promise chain of the `fetch` result, so a `fetch` option that threw synchronously left the timer running. When the request was then retried, the stale timer fired mid-flight and aborted the shared `AbortController`, cancelling the new attempt or its body read. The timer is now cleared in a `finally` block so it is always released.

ky.query: Timeouts and user aborts do not stop a request returned by beforeRequest or beforeRetry hooks.
ky.query_en: Fix timeouts and user aborts not cancelling a `Request` returned from `beforeRequest` or `beforeRetry` hooks A fresh `Request` returned from these hooks carried its own signal, so Ky's managed signal never reached the fetch. User `signal` aborts left the request pending forever, and per-attempt, body-read, and total timeouts threw `TimeoutError` without cancelling the in-flight fetch. The returned request now gets the managed signal re-attached, the same way `ky.retry({request})` already did. Only `Request` instances get the managed signal; `Request`-like objects are used as-is since the `Requ

ky.query: Extending an instance with retry options as an object, and then with a number, loses the other retry options.
ky.query_en: Fix extending an object `retry` with a number dropping the other retry options

ky.query: When extending an instance, overriding or removing an HTTP header written with different casing does not work, even though header names are case-insensitive.
ky.query_en: Fix header overrides and removals in `.extend()` ignoring header name case with plain objects HTTP header names are case-insensitive, but merging plain header objects used key-sensitive object spreading. Setting a header with a different spelling kept both entries, so the earlier value could win or both were sent, and deleting with `undefined` did nothing unless the spelling matched exactly. Merged plain header objects now keep lowercase keys, like `Headers` does, so overrides and `undefined` deletions match regardless of spelling and `init` hooks can rely on lowercase keys like `options.heade

ky.query: beforeError hooks run twice when the response body fails after its reading has already timed out.
ky.query_en: Fix `beforeError` hooks running again when a body fails after the body read timed out The network error wrapping for body reads was attached to the body promise itself, so a body that failed after the timeout had already won the race processed the discarded error and ran `beforeError` hooks a second time in the background. The wrapping now happens only on the awaited path.

ky.query: The type of the function that decides whether to retry rejects functions that return nothing.
ky.query_en: Fix `shouldRetry` type rejecting functions that return nothing

ky.query: A header set to undefined in an init hook is sent as the word 'undefined'.
ky.query_en: Fix headers set to `undefined` in `init` hooks being sent as the string `"undefined"` Headers modified by `init` hooks skip the option merging that filters `undefined` values, and the `Headers` constructor turns `undefined` into the string `'undefined'`, so `options.headers.foo = undefined` in an `init` hook sent `foo: undefined` instead of removing the header. Plain header objects are now applied entry by entry so `undefined` deletes the header, matching the documented behavior for `.extend()`.

ky.query: If the connection drops while reading the response body with the JSON or text shortcuts, the raw runtime error is thrown instead of a network error.
ky.query_en: Fix a connection dropped while reading the body through shortcuts surfacing as a raw `TypeError` When the connection dropped while `.json()`, `.text()`, or another shortcut was reading the response body, the runtime's raw `TypeError` (for example, `terminated` from undici) escaped unchanged, so `isNetworkError()` was false and `beforeError` hooks were skipped, unlike body-read timeouts which are processed. Such errors are now wrapped in `NetworkError` with the original error as `cause` and run through `beforeError`. They are still not retried, matching body-read timeouts.

ky.query: When setting query parameters, options taken from a Request object passed as input, like credentials, cache and redirect, are lost.
ky.query_en: Fix `searchParams` dropping request options inherited from a `Request` input When `searchParams` is set, the request is rebuilt with the new URL from the options alone, so `credentials`, `cache`, `redirect`, `integrity`, `referrer`, and `referrerPolicy` set on a `Request` input were reset to their defaults. In browsers this silently stopped sending cookies for `credentials: 'include'` requests. The rebuilt request now reads those options back from the request that was already constructed, so inherited values survive and explicit options still win.

ky.query: In init hooks the context is undefined when not passed, even though the documentation says it is always an object.
ky.query_en: Fix `context` being `undefined` in `init` hooks The `context` option is documented to be available in all hooks and to always be an object, but `init` hooks received the raw options where a missing `context` stayed `undefined`, so `options.context.key = value` threw. Init hooks now get an empty object when no context was provided, matching every other hook.

ky.query: The custom JSON parser is ignored when reading JSON from a cloned copy of the response.
ky.query_en: Fix `parseJson` being ignored by `response.clone().json()` The custom `json()` was set as an own property on the response, so every clone fell back to the native parser. This affected `response.clone()` on the returned response, on the streamed `onDownloadProgress` response, and on the response passed to `afterResponse` hooks. Clones are now decorated too and keep the same request context.

ky.query: Abort does not propagate to retries, and uploads do not work where the request does not support streaming.
ky.query_en: Fix retry abort propagation and uploads without request stream support

ky.query: JSON error responses are not correctly decoded as UTF-8.
ky.query_en: Fix UTF-8 decoding of JSON error responses

ky.query: When merging JSON objects, old elements remain in arrays.
ky.query_en: Fix stale array entries when merging JSON objects

ky.query: In retries and hooks, thrown values that are not Error objects must be preserved as they are.
ky.query_en: Preserve non-Error values in retry errors and hooks

ky.query: The return type of the bytes shortcut is not compatible with Blob and Response.
ky.query_en: Fix bytes shortcut return type for Blob and Response compatibility

ky.query: Abort reasons must be preserved while reading the body of an HTTP error response.
ky.query_en: Preserve abort reasons while reading HTTP error bodies

ky.query: Avoid rebuilding the request when unnecessary, report zero when the total size is unknown, and fix two old tests.
ky.query_en: Skip a needless request rebuild, report an unknown total as zero, and fix two stale tests

ky.query: If the progress callback throws something that is not an Error, that too must not cause the request to be retried.
ky.query_en: Make a non-Error progress-callback throw non-retriable too

ky.query: An error thrown in the beforeRetry hook from another JavaScript realm, like an iframe or a worker, is not recognized; the original error must be kept as the cause.
ky.query_en: Recognise a cross-realm `beforeRetry` error and keep the retried error as the cause
